chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you do not know whether you have prayed two or four, and your doubt does not lean towards anything specific, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām, then pray two Rak'at and four Sajdahs, reciting Umm al-Qur'an in both of them, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām. So if you had only prayed two, these two would complete the four, and if you had prayed four, these two would be optional (Nafl).

And if you do not know whether you have prayed three or four, and your doubt does not lean towards anything specific, then offer the Salām, then pray two Rak'at while you are seated, reciting in them Umm al-Kitab. And if your doubt leans towards the three, then stand and pray the fourth Rak'ah and do not perform the two Sajdahs of forgetfulness. So if your doubt leans towards the four, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām, then perform the two Sajdahs of forgetfulness.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for completing prayer when unsure if you prayed two, three, or four Rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential methodology for resolving uncertainty (Shakk) in obligatory prayers, distinguishing between neutral doubt and doubt leaning towards a specific number. It establishes the principle of 'building on certainty' (Al-Istishab) by prescribing distinct corrective actions, such as completing the prayer or performing Sajdah al-Sahw, to ensure validity without excessive burden. This reflects the Shia emphasis on practical ease (Taysir) while maintaining ritual precision in daily worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you do not know whether you have prayed two (Rak’at) or four and your imagination does not go to anything, so perform Tashahhud and offer Salām. Then pray two Rak’at (of Salāt) and four Sujūd (plural of Sajdah), reciting in both of these with the Mother of the Quran (Chapter 1), then perform Tashahhud and offer Salām. So if it was so, that rather you had prayed two Rak’at, these two would complete the four, and if you had prayed four, these two would be (counted as) optional (Salāt).

And if you did not know whether you had prayed three or four, and your imagination does not go towards anything, so offer Salām, then pray two Rak’at while you are seated, reciting in these two with the Mother of the Book (Chapter 1). And if your imagination goes towards the three (Rak’at having been prayed), so stand and pray the fourth Rak’at and do not perform Sajdah with the Sajdah of the omission. So if your imagination goes towards the four (Rak’at having been prayed), so perform Tashahhud and offer Salām, then perform Sajdah with the Sajdah of the omission’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abdullah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

You may not know whether you have performed two or four Rak’ah and your guess about one side is not greater than the other side. You must say Tashahhud (testimonies of belief) and Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace), then perform two Rak’ah and four Sujud (prostrations). Read in them ‘ Umm al-Quran, then say Tashahhud (testimonies of belief) and Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace). If, in fact, you had performed two Rak’ah these two complete the four and if, in fact, you had performed four, these two become optional.

If you do not know whether you have performed three or four Rak’ah and your guess about one side is not greater than the other; say Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace), then perform two Rak’ah in a sitting position. Read in them al-Fatihah al-Kitab. If your guess about three is greater, then perform the fourth Rak’ah. Do not perform two Sajdah (prostration) because of mistake. If your guess about four is greater; say Tashahhud (testimonies of belief) and Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) then perform two Sajdah (prostration) because of mistake.’”
